ultrasonics pretreated lignocellulosic substrates can be more easily biodegraded by white rot fungi than untreated substrates.

the combination of ultrasonic treatment with white rot fungi enzymes can enhance the biodegradation of lignocellulosic materials, which is a promising strategy to improve the efficiency of the enzymatic hydrolysis of lignocelluloses.
the combination of ultrasound pretreatment and enzyme extracts from the white rot fungi P. chrysosporum or Trametes resulted in enhanced degradation of lignocellulosic wheat chaff.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel process for the biodegradation of lignocellulosic materials using a combination of ultrasound and enzyme extracts obtained from white rot fungi.
the development of an environmentally friendly and cost effective process for the conversion of lignocellulosic materials to value-added products.
the development of an environmentally friendly process for the production of biofuels from lignocellulosic waste materials.

ultrasound treatment of wheat chaff prior to treatment with white rot fungal enzyme extracts increased the concentration of sugars produced and the concentration of lignins degradation products obtained from wheat chalf after enzyme addition.
the use of ultrasound pretreatment in conjunction with white rot fungi enzymes is a promising strategy for lignocellulose biodegradation.

ultrasound treatment is an effective pretreatment for the enzymatic hydrolysis of wheat chaff and that the use of a combined enzyme system is more effective for the hydrolysis of the pretreated biomass.

the use of a combination of ultrasound and white rot fungi is a promising approach for the biodegradation of lignocellulosic materials.
the combination of ultrasonic pretreatment with white rot fungi enzyme extracts can improve the biodegradability of lignocellulosic materials.
ultrasound treatment of lignocellulosic materials prior to enzymatic hydrolysis enhances the release of sugars and degradation of lignin.

ultrasound treatment of wheat chaff prior to enzyme addition can be used for the pretreatment of lignocellulosic materials for biofuel production.
ultrasound pretreatment can improve the efficiency of enzymatic hydrolysis of lignocellulosic materials.
ultrasonic pretreatment can be used to increase the efficiency of enzymatic hydrolysis of wheat chaff by white rot fungi.
